tagline: From Killdeer into the badlands, losing an hour at the river.
intro: Killdeer began in 1914 at the end of a Northern Pacific branch line and took its name from the Killdeer Mountains, two flat-topped buttes off to the northwest. ND 22 heads north out of town past them, and twelve miles on it enters the badlands. Then it crosses the Little Missouri River, and the clocks change from Mountain to Central time.
The town's Hidatsa name means Where-Deer-Are-Killed, and the buttes were a deer hunting ground before they were a battlefield.

moments.title: Killdeer Mountain Battlefield
moments.text: In July 1864 General Alfred Sully advanced 2,200 soldiers on foot in a hollow square against a large Sioux encampment under the buttes, part of the largest Army expedition ever sent against Native Americans.

moments.title: Little Missouri River
moments.text: The highway crosses a river that rises near Devils Tower in Wyoming and carries the eroded badlands downstream, and on the far bank the time is Central.
